evidence.note: Before writing any training code, agent measured bytes-per-token and probed int8 zlib compression ratio — treating size feasibility as an explicit up-front checkpoint that de-risks the byte cap.
Smoke-tested the end-to-end training pipeline at small scale first, iterating on compile issues, rather than launching a big run monolithically — a working-pipeline milestone before scaling.
Explicit size-under-budget done-checks (verify checkpoint size after dedup; verify size with mlp_mult=3) locked size correctness as a gate before committing to a full run.
Measured throughput/compute cost, then launched the full training run only after smoke test + size gates passed — clear phase ordering baseline→scale.
After the run, estimated params/size for deeper models and measured actual checkpoint sizes before scaling, showing capacity↔size trade-off handled as ordered decisions rather than a fresh gamble.

reasoning: The observable action sequence shows a genuine baseline-first decomposition with ordered phases and concrete done-checks: size-feasibility probe and smoke test before scaling, explicit <32MB size gates locked before capacity scaling, throughput measured for compute planning, then val monitoring and size re-estimation before deeper models — exceeding level 5's 'rough success criteria' and approaching level 8's explicit gates sequenced so size correctness precedes scaling. It falls short of a clean 8 because the visible gates cover size/smoke/throughput/val_bpb but not an explicit grader-interface load or forward-contract test in the titles, and lacks the explicit fallback-branch frontier management of level 10, placing it at 7.
